title: Game systems and prototype
description: Design scoped mechanics, model balance when relevant, build requested prototypes, and check actual playtest/quality evidence.
intent: Complete the requested game design, prototype, or balance assessment against the intended player experience. Do not invent fun, retention, telemetry, real playtests, or production economy changes.

assignments.task: Establish experience goals, rules, loops, state transitions, tuning parameters, constraints, and acceptance/playtest hypotheses.
Review consequential economy/probability/balance models and numerical assumptions.
assignments.when: The mechanics rely on nontrivial quantitative models.
Consequential engine or structural choices are involved.
The scope includes a user-facing interface or input flow.

assignments.task: Assess asset/shader/rendering integration constraints and budgets.
assignments.when: Visual runtime integration affects the requested scope.

assignments.task: Implement only the requested bounded game prototype or tuning change with reproducible fixtures and applicable checks.
assignments.when: The user requests prototype implementation or scoped source/tuning changes.

assignments.task: Assess completed design/prototype and actual supplied or authorized local playtest evidence; distinguish predictions from observed experience.
Review applicable correctness, edge states, deterministic checks, and regressions.
assignments.when: A runnable prototype or changed source is available.

assignments.task: Verify relevant measured budgets using comparable scenes/workloads.
assignments.when: Performance budgets or claims matter to the prototype.

assignments.task: Analyze actual approved gameplay telemetry/results without inventing players or enjoyment.
Check material balance/probability/experience claims against completed evidence.
assignments.when: The deliverable makes consequential quantitative or empirical claims.

completion: The bounded design/prototype and requested checks are complete against explicit experience goals.
Real observations, simulations, models, and predicted experience are distinguished.
Implementation is serialized and no real-user study, live economy, monetization, or publication is inferred.
